releases.notes:
MinecraftModConventions 3.5.0

**3.5.0 adds the [recording rules](https://github.com/brainage04/MinecraftModConventions/blob/v3.5.0/README.md#shooting-a-recording).** `showStep` and `showStepAndHold` fail a caption that says what was removed or changed, so a mod whose captions do that fails its client GameTests until it rewords them. Recordings show every particle (`particles:0`), and `GTR_RECORDING_FPS=60` records the video at 60 frames a second on a card display, where the client's frame cap follows the capture rate; a client that cannot draw 60 presents fewer, and the measured 60 fps take presented 43.6 frames a second and repeated 997 of its 2816 video frames. A recording now captures the game's own picture and sound (`GTR_RECORDING_CAPTURE=game`, see [Client GameTest recording](https://github.com/brainage04/MinecraftModConventions/blob/v3.5.0/README.md#client-gametest-recording)): the client copies each finished frame out of its render target and plays its sound into an OpenAL loopback device, so every video frame is one whole picture, none can tear, and the machine plays no sound. `GTR_RECORDING_CAPTURE=x11grab` grabs the screen as before, and on a card display such a take replaces the frames x11grab tears with the frame before each. It also replaces a frame where the screen changed below a line one capture before it changed above it, such as a chat bar opening whose suggestion list appears above it a capture later, which repeats the previous picture for one frame. On a 25-minute TwitchPlaysMinecraft take it replaced 134 of 46,156 frames, tears and such frames together. A tear on a frame where the caption or another overlay also changes can go unrepaired and unreported. New checks can fail a recording: an x11grab card take that still has a torn frame after that repair fails unless `GTR_RECORDING_TEAR_CHECK=warn`, a `GTR_RECORDING_FPS` above 30 that gets the virtual display fails before the client starts, an encoder that cannot encode a test frame fails before the client starts, and a game take fails on a graphics backend other than OpenGL, on an OpenAL without `ALC_SOFT_loopback`, or when its capture stops mid-take; `GTR_RECORDING_CAPTURE=x11grab` is the fallback for the last three. Every recording whose mod keeps MinecraftModConventions' caption panel shows a [performance overlay](https://github.com/brainage04/MinecraftModConventions/blob/v3.5.0/README.md#shooting-a-recording) under it, which a test can move or hide with `ClientGameTestRecorder.placePerformanceOverlay`, and keeps its numbers as `perf*` values in the metadata. `GTR_RECORDING_VIDEO_ENCODER=h264_nvenc` encodes the capture on an NVIDIA card, and `GTR_RECORDING_TRACE=true` writes the time of every present beside the boundaries. Self-hosted runners now use SDL's EGL path too, which Minecraft 26.3 clients need there, so a self-hosted runner needs EGL installed (`libegl1` and `libegl-mesa0`).

releases.notes:
Release 3.3.0: warn-only source checks for vanilla identities

3.1.x-3.3.x target Minecraft 26.3; 3.0.x stays the Minecraft 26.2 line.

- checkVanillaIdentity (under check) reports hardcoded vanilla dimension
  identities (Level.OVERWORLD/NETHER/END) in main and client sources to
  build/reports/vanilla-identity.txt and warns; it no longer fails the
  build. The guidance asks whether the code is about that place by name
  or about a property the game reads from data (BED_RULE,
  WATER_EVAPORATES, ...).
- checkVanillaTagIdentities reports comparisons with a specific vanilla
  block, item or biome where a vanilla tag names it (red_bed and
  #minecraft:beds), reading the tags from the project's own Minecraft
  jars, to build/reports/vanilla-tag-identities.txt.
- checkWorldHeight reports hardcoded build limits (-64, 319, 320, 0/256
  in a Y context) to build/reports/world-height.txt.
- All three only warn; `// <marker>: <reason>` silences a line.
- The NeoForge server install runs the installer from the cache instead
  of copying it.
- scripts/trim_stages.py cuts a client GameTest recording to its
  STAGE_START/STAGE_END stages and writes each clip's frame range.

releases.notes:
Release 3.2.0: client GameTests against a vanilla server

3.1.x/3.2.x target Minecraft 26.3; 3.0.x stays the Minecraft 26.2 line.

- runVanillaServerClientGameTest (production-gametests; :fabric: in a
  multi-loader mod) downloads Mojang's dedicated server jar for
  minecraft_version once, checked against its SHA-1, starts it offline,
  flat and in creative on a free local port, and runs the production
  client GameTests against it. It fails when no client joined the
  server. It is not part of runAllGameTests.
- VanillaServerClientGameTests.checkCreativeItems checks that a mod
  which registers items keeps them out of creative on a server without
  it and that taking one does not get the player kicked, then sends the
  held-back set_creative_mode_slot packet and expects the decode kick.
  withVanillaServer and assertConnected serve other checks.

releases.notes:
Release 3.1.2: client GameTests on GitHub-hosted runners

3.1.x targets Minecraft 26.3; 3.0.x stays the Minecraft 26.2 line.

- On GitHub-hosted runners, reusable-client-gametests.yml and
  reusable-production-gametests.yml set SDL_VIDEO_FORCE_EGL=1 for the
  steps that start a client, and install libegl1 and libegl-mesa0.
  Minecraft 26.3 asks SDL3 for an sRGB-capable framebuffer, and Ubuntu
  24.04's Xvfb offers no sRGB-capable GLX visual, so every client
  GameTest failed with "Couldn't find matching GLX visual" before any
  test ran. Self-hosted runners keep SDL's default GLX path.

releases.notes:
Release 3.1.1: recorded production clients in single-loader projects

3.1.x targets Minecraft 26.3; 3.0.x stays the Minecraft 26.2 line.

- With client-gametest-recorder and production-gametests applied
  together, the recorded production client uses the recorder's display
  and audio sink instead of its own Xvfb and OpenAL's null driver, in
  single-loader projects as well as through
  multiloader-mod-conventions. Before, a single-loader recording of the
  production client was silent and its window was on a display the
  recorder did not capture.

releases.notes:
Release 3.1.0: Minecraft 26.3

3.1.x targets Minecraft 26.3; 3.0.x stays the Minecraft 26.2 line.

- Toolchain: Gradle 9.8.2, Fabric Loom 1.19.3, Architectury Loom 1.17.493,
  Fabric Loader 0.19.5, Fabric API 0.165.0+26.3, NeoForge 26.3.0.99.
- The recorder mixin follows GpuSurface to com.mojang.renderpearl.
- On Linux, automated client launches (client GameTests, Loom GameTest
  runs, the recorder) use SDL's X11 driver and drop WAYLAND_DISPLAY:
  Minecraft 26.3 opens its window through SDL3, which otherwise prefers
  a Wayland desktop over Xvfb. Interactive runs are left alone.
- A client launch that ends before the client finished loading (for
  example, no window) now fails with an explanation, whatever its exit
  code.
- Recorded runs open a window as large as the recorder display instead of
  fullscreen, which SDL3 cannot do on Xvfb.
- options.txt carries 26.3's data version (5023) and a valid
  maxAnisotropyBit (1).

releases.notes:
Release 3.0.2

Recordings no longer freeze when the disk or memory is busy: the raw
capture's muxer queues 4096 packets, so writes that wait on the ext4
journal cannot stop x11grab, and a recording job in a limited cgroup of
its own is protected from sibling reclaim with memory.low.
